insights.claim: The gateway delegates all authentication enforcement to upstream infrastructure and the backend orchestrator, forwarding Authorization headers without inspection.
insights.reasoning: The gateway only forwards Authorization and x-forwarded-* headers to the orchestrator. No token validation, RBAC check, or rate limiting is performed at the gateway layer. This means the gateway must be deployed behind a platform-level authentication proxy or service mesh to prevent unauthenticated access.

insights.claim: TLS to the orchestrator backend is conditionally enabled based on certificate file presence, creating a dual HTTP/HTTPS operational mode.
insights.reasoning: The build_orchestrator_client function checks for TLS cert, key, and CA files at well-known mount paths. When present, it constructs an mTLS identity via OpenSSL PKCS#12; when absent, it falls back to plain HTTP. This pattern supports both development (no TLS) and production (mTLS via platform-injected certs) deployments, but means the encryption state is determined at runtime by file system state rather than explicit configuration.

insights.claim: The gateway implements route-level content safety policy through a fallback message mechanism that replaces model output when detections are triggered.
insights.reasoning: Each route can define a fallback_message in its configuration. When the orchestrator returns detection results, the gateway replaces model output with this fallback text. This provides operators a per-route safety override without modifying the orchestrator or model behavior, but the policy is binary (replace all or nothing) rather than graduated.
